purpose: Source-backed control geometry for the Chicago River bend and the two southern rail bascules. This file is an audit input, not a replacement scene generator.

coordinate_frame.axes: X east, Y north, Z up
coordinate_frame.projection: x = (lon - lon0) * 111320 * cos(lat0) + home_offset_x + registration_x; y = (lat - lat0) * 110900 + home_offset_y
coordinate_frame.registration_rule: Apply the +33 m X registration exactly once to raw tangent-projected OSM/Hydro points. Do not add it again when consuming this file's local_xy_m values.

sources.name: City of Chicago Hydro dataset
sources.role: Bank polygon and scanline width authority. Coordinates were transformed through the shared tangent projection and registration.
sources.raw_geometry_artifact_contents: 44 downloaded WGS84 MultiPolygon features selected by properties.name, with source properties and coordinates preserved.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap waterway geometry via Overpass
sources.role: Centerline control points used to expose the northward bend. OSM is map geometry, not a survey.

sources.name: Library of Congress HAER, St. Charles Air Line Bridge
sources.role: Historical bridge identity, location and source-photo orientation.

sources.name: City of Chicago landmarks record, St. Charles Air Line Bridge
sources.role: Current landmark context and address north of 16th Street, east of Lumber Street.

centerline_control_points.label: south approach to B&OCT / St. Charles
St. Charles Air Line bridge centerline

model_comparison.finding: The current slab is a straight staging rectangle while the mapped river moves from x~173 at y=-504 to x~155 at Roosevelt and x~-110 at the Willis latitude. It cannot simultaneously establish the river edge, bridge banks, powerhouse relation and north skyline geography.

bridge_control.finding: At y=-393 the Hydro bank interval is approximately x=140..201 and the OSM bridge centerline is x~171.3. The eastern pivot near x=202 is therefore a plausible east-bank mechanism location; the apparent wrong-bank issue is caused by the straight channel and competing legacy overlays.
